title: The two connected quandles of order 6 colour every knot equally
claim: Target: let K be a knot in S3 with group pi, exterior X, meridian mu and preferred longitude lambda. (a) Every homomorphism rho: pi -> S4 with rho(mu) a transposition t has rho(lambda) = 1. Reason: rho lifts through the central extension {+I, -I} -> GL(2,3) -> PGL(2,3) = S4, because the obstruction lies in H^2(pi; F2) = 0 (equivalently, one Wirtinger relator follows from the others); lambda lies in the commutator subgroup and commutes with mu, so rho(lambda) is 1 or the double transposition z commuting with t, and every pair of lifts of t and z anticommutes. (b) Let phi: pi -> S3 send mu to the image of t, and let V be V4 with S3 acting by conjugation, a self-dual module. By half-lives-half-dies the image of H^1(X; V) in the 2-dimensional space H^1(boundary of X; V) is a line, and by (a) it is not the line of classes that vanish on the meridian. Hence evaluation at the meridian maps the lifting cocycles onto V4: for a fixed 4-cycle c over the image of t, the lifts of phi with rho(mu) = t and with rho(mu) = c are equinumerous, and all lifts with rho(mu) = c share one longitude in {1, c^2}. (c) Consequently every knot has as many colourings by the transposition conjugation quandle of S4 as by the 4-cycle conjugation quandle; these are the connected quandles C[6,1] = G(Z2, 0) and C[6,2] = G(Z2, 1), so their counts agree on every knot, as Clark, Elhamdadi, Hou, Saito and Yeatman conjectured in 2013 for this pair. Every knot with a non-trivial Fox 3-colouring has a non-trivial C[6,2] colouring, as Carter, Oshiro and Saito conjectured in 2009.
failure_conditions: A knot with a transposition colouring whose longitude is not 1, or a pair of lifts to GL(2,3) of a transposition and of its commuting double transposition that commute.

An S3 colouring of a knot whose numbers of lifts with a fixed transposition meridian and with a fixed 4-cycle meridian differ, whose 4-cycle lifts have two different longitudes, or whose boundary restriction image is not one-dimensional.
A knot whose colouring counts by the two conjugation quandles differ, or a failure of the identification of C[6,1] and C[6,2] with these quandles.
A virtual-knot control under which the equality cannot fail.
foundation_claim_scope: Classical knots in S3, not links or virtual knots; colouring counts by the two connected quandles of order 6. Cited, not proved: Poincare-Lefschetz duality with local coefficients, asphericity of knot exteriors or the redundancy of one Wirtinger relator, and S4 = PGL(2,3). The other pairs of Galkin quandles in the 2013 conjecture are not covered. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof (cited: Poincare-Lefschetz duality and universal coefficients with local coefficients, asphericity of knot exteriors, S4 = PGL(2,3)); check.py (standard library, under 1 s) verifies the GL(2,3) anticommutation of lifts of a transposition and its commuting double transposition, the identification of the Galkin quandles G(Z2,0), G(Z2,1) with the transposition and 4-cycle quandles, and on 27 knots (braid closures, alternating and tripled alternating diagrams, connected sums, random braids) by brute force: trivial transposition longitudes, equal lift counts for all four meridian values over every S3 colouring with one longitude each, equal totals, non-trivial 4-cycle colourings of 3-colourable knots; controls: a virtual knot breaks the equality (5 against 1), longitudes take both values. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with finite checks
